_comment: SALVAGE kit: the re-plated cell. Bare scrap steel welded down over a grimy hull, and the piece that carries the look at a distance. Its long axis is X, so `align: Run` lays it ACROSS the run instead of down it - the deliberate misalignment the look is built on. Nothing is centred: the sheet overhangs +Z, the full-length bead runs one edge only, and the bolts sit at three irregular spots, so a row of them reads as separate repairs rather than as a repeating tile. Two budget notes, both deliberate. FOOTPRINT is 0.9 of a cell, not the default half: a greeble is always stood at the CENTRE of its plate, so the half-cell default guards against a jitter the scatter does not have, and at 0.9 two of these on neighbouring plates JOIN into one re-skinned band instead of reading as two stickers. That width also means the sheet does not sit flush on a plate that falls away - a piece is lifted to its plate's MEAN height, so on a `Brink` one end stands proud. That is kept ON PURPOSE. A repair that does not quite lie down is what a repair looks like; a perfectly bedded one looks like trim.
